title: Nearly 1,400 Workers Lose Jobs at an Ohio Truck Factory
summary:
Nearly 1,400 people lost their jobs on Wednesday, September 30, at a truck factory in Springfield, Ohio. The plant had been known as the Navistar factory.

A layoff means an employer ends a worker's job. For families, losing a steady paycheck can make everyday costs harder to manage. One affected worker, Kyle Bos, has two daughters and another child due in January. He described concerns about rising grocery prices as well as losing his job.

The layoffs were large enough to roughly cancel out an entire year of job growth in the greater Dayton area. They happened three days before President Donald Trump's Saturday rally nearby.

Dayton has a long history of making and inventing things. The Wright brothers' airplane and the electric car starter were among inventions developed there. But the region has lost about half of the 90,000 factory jobs it had in 1990, according to federal figures.

Other kinds of work have grown. Wright-Patterson Air Force Base now directly employs 38,000 people. Its work has helped attract aerospace companies, which develop aircraft and related technology.

The White House pointed to company investments as evidence that its policies are creating jobs. Jeff Hoagland, who leads the Dayton Development Coalition, said building an economy takes time. The factory layoffs show the difficulties some families still face.
why_it_matters: Jobs provide income for families. The layoffs help readers understand how families can face difficulties even while other businesses in their region grow.
